transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-04-06
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Venture Medical - Head of ML), David Ortiz (Venture Medical - Platform Eng), Sara Lee (Venture Medical - Security)

Summary: quick weekly check-in on the POC results, model selection and pinning choices, and next steps for benchmarks and security review. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, fallback models for rolling back, and on-prem readiness.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do a quick 30 minute sync then dive into the benchmark numbers priya has, and then action items, sound good?
[00:12] Laura (Venture Medical): yep, sounds good, we got David and sara on too.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): hi team, hi laura, quick note I'm on wifi so if i cut, i'll repop. ok jumping in, so since last week we ran the 2 model tracks you asked for: a quantized 13b from our catalog (v1.2-q4) and the 70b float baseline (v2.0).
[00:36] David (Venture Medical): quick q, v1.2-q4 is that the one with the new kv cache changes?
[00:41] Priya: yeah it's the one with the K V cache prefix optimizations — though the transcript here might say K V cash sometimes — but yes, tighter kv cache hits for prompt reuse.
[00:51] Laura: we care a lot about 95th pct latency, and also cost per call. the 70b looked better on quality but cost was pretty high.
[00:59] Priya: exactly. numbers — these are median/95th and tokens/sec for the two pinned candidates:
[01:06] Priya: v1.2-q4 (quant): median latency 220ms for our 256-token prompts, 95th ~480ms on hosted pool, throughput 120 tok/s; cost est $0.004 per call (normalized).
[01:22] Priya: v2.0 (70b float): median 140ms, 95th 320ms, throughput 210 tok/s; cost est $0.012 per call.
[01:33] Laura: okay so 3x cost difference roughly, with quality delta — can you remind us the eval accuracy numbers?
[01:38] Priya: from the 20 eval prompts you provided last week, v2.0 had 93% pass on our rubric, v1.2-q4 had 88% with a few hallucination cases on long context. there were specific prompt classes — boundary conditions and table extraction — where quant had trouble.
[01:56] David: do we have rollback/fallback paths? like if we pin to the quantized model for cost, can we auto-fallback to v2.0 on low-confidence outputs?
[02:03] Alex: yes, that's the recommended pattern — pin primary to v1.2-q4 for cost and set routed fallback to v2.0 for low-likelihood or for specific routes. we can also do percent-based canary or per-route overrides.
[02:15] Sara (Security): on the security side, i'm still worried about data residency and KMS — do we have audit logs when routing falls back to another model?
[02:23] Priya: yes, we emit per-request trace and model route metadata to the console, logs include model id, route, and policy decision. those can be shipped to your SIEM or S3. also works with customer KMS for key rotations.
[02:36] Laura: great. a couple of questions: 1) if we pin v1.2-q4 and it degrades for certain prompt classes, how fast is rollback? is that manual only?
[02:45] Priya: rollback can be manual in the console (one click) or automated via our rollout policy; you can configure thresholds — e.g., if eval fail rate > X or latency spike > Y then automatic rollback to prior model/version. latency to change is seconds for routing, but full warmup may take minutes depending on cold KV cache.
[03:03] David: the warmup/cold cache is a concern for us — our traffic burst is often new user queries which don't hit cache. how do you manage that for on-prem?
[03:12] Priya: for Dedicated or Private we recommend a small warm-up pool or pre-warming script, and we support scheduled prefetch for top N prefixes. if that's not possible, you can use staged rollout and keep a small % on float model to catch errors while cache populates.
[03:29] Alex: to add, we can also do batching tweaks — increase batching window slightly to improve throughput on cold caches at the expense of a bit more latency for single-shot calls.
[03:39] Laura: what's your recommendation for our profile (50k calls/day, 90% single-shot prompts)?
[03:45] Priya: I'd recommend primary v1.2-q4 pinned for most routes, with v2.0 fallback for the top 10% most sensitive routes (table extraction, billing answers). also run a 50k token throughput benchmark under pinned configuration to validate tail latencies — we'll do that next week.
[04:00] Laura: okay. on the catalog naming, can you confirm model ids? we've seen conflicting names in the docs vs the console.
[04:06] Alex: sorry for confusion — in the console it's labeled redwood/v1.2-q4 and redwood/v2.0-full70. the catalog docs earlier had redwood-70b which is older naming, we've updated the docs but i'll send a short mapping table.
[04:19] David: fantastic, please include the quantization/precision details in that mapping — we need to explain to infra why memory and GPU sizing differ.
[04:26] Priya: noted — i'll include memory footprint, expected GPU type (A10G vs H100 depending on float/quant), and recommended batch sizes.
[04:34] Sara: for SOC2 and KMS headers, also need to know where logs with model decisions reside and retention controls. are these configurable per-customer?
[04:42] Priya: yes retention and log destinations are configurable; for Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem with your KMS; for hosted we offer encrypted logs with customer-managed keys in supported regions.
[04:52] Laura: good. one last technical: for the fallback, can the system do a delta compare and surface differences to our telemetry so we can see why the fallback was triggered?
[04:59] Priya: we provide request/response diffs in the tracing console and will annotate with reason codes (low confidence, safety filter hit, model error). there's also an API to stream those events.
[05:10] Alex: ok next, quick review of the pilot timeline — week 1 baseline tests done, week 2 pinning experiment in progress, week 3 production sim and SLA verification, week 4 decision. you're currently at start of week 2.
[05:24] Laura: sounds right. our internal timeline wants a go/no-go by 2027-04-20 for procurement.
[05:30] Alex: noted. we'll prioritize the benchmark and security docs.
[05:34] David: one more thing — cost controls: can we limit total spend and auto-throttle or change model routing when cost threshold hits?
[05:41] Priya: yes, we have per-route and global cost guards — you can set budget caps that will either slow down batching, switch routes to lower-cost model, or return a soft-fail error. we'll show config examples.
[05:52] Laura: OK. any blockers from our side?
[05:55] Laura: we need to share the eval prompts (we'll upload today), and Sara will share the redacted security spec.
[06:02] Alex: perfect. we'll consolidate into a follow-up email.
[06:06] Priya: action items recap — i'll run the 50k token throughput test pinned to v1.2-q4 and collect tail latency traces, i'll also run a fallback simulation to see time-to-fallback and cache warmup impact.
[06:19] Laura: that covers it. thanks Alex and priya.
[06:23] Alex: thanks all, i'll send pricing + SOW + mapping table by Friday.
[06:28] Sara: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
